title: SwinIR: Image Restoration Using Swin Transformer
grouping: The overview fills the top row; two detail panels share the bottom row, captioned (a) and (b). In the overview the deep stage is a grey rounded container with a bold title ('Deep Feature Extraction'); the other stages stand alone. Detail panel (a) has a pale-blue background matching the blocks it opens and is tied to the first of them by grey dashed zoom lines; panel (b) has a pale-yellow background matching the sub-blocks drawn in (a).
shapes_depth: The shallow-feature and reconstruction stages are flat trapezoids (pale green narrowing, peach widening) with bold names; repeated blocks are tall narrow upright boxes with rotated labels. The global residual is a curved line passing under the deep container to a circled +; inside the detail panels residuals are curved underpasses to circled +. Saturated fills appear only in (b) (green LayerNorm, red MSA, orange MLP) and cyan for Conv. The input is a tiny low-resolution photo on the far left; the output is a much larger photo on the far right.
proposed_highlight: The proposed blocks are expanded two levels deep (block to layer), each detail panel tinted with the fill of the box it opens.
lesson: State the super-resolution task by size alone - a tiny low-resolution photo on the left, a several-times larger output photo on the right - and nest detail panels two levels deep, each tinted with the fill of the block it opens.
notes: Venue not verified here (remembered as ICCV Workshops 2021), so venue = arXiv and year = arXiv preprint year.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
